summary:
AETHRION // MARS – Mars Mission Control & Astronaut Navigation System

AETHRION // MARS is an interactive planetary exploration and mission-planning platform designed to help future astronauts explore the Martian surface safely and efficiently. It integrates scientific datasets from NASA missions and instruments, including HiRISE, MOLA, InSight and MEDA, into a unified exploration environment.

The platform combines high-resolution orbital imagery, elevation and slope mapping, environmental information, geological hazard detection and A* multi-objective route optimisation. Astronauts can explore Mars in an interactive 3D planetary environment, identify scientific sampling targets, assess terrain risks, simulate surface traverses and generate mission dossiers.

By bringing multiple sources of planetary science data together, AETHRION // MARS addresses the challenge of making complex Martian information accessible and actionable for human exploration. It is important because future Mars missions will require informed decisions about navigation, astronaut safety, resource limitations and scientific discovery. Our goal is to help transform planetary data into practical mission intelligence for the next generation of explorers.
details:
PROJECT SPECIFICATION – AETHRION // MARS

1. What does your project do?

AETHRION // MARS is an interactive system, which can be used to aid in planning future human exploration missions on Mars. By integrating various forms of scientific and geographical information related to Mars, AETHRION can be used to provide insight into the terrain whilst identifying any hazards, highlighting valuable scientific sites and help plan surface exploration missions.

The system includes a simulated walking mission across Mars at Jezero Crater, which is a scientifically valuable area of Mars.

The system allows the user to explore Mars with an immersive 3D experience. Once in mission control they will be able to explore the Martian terrain, see different geographical layers and gain knowledge of the environment of Mars. They will have access to:

Multiple NASA science data and mission information such as HiRISE images, MOLA topography, InSight observations, MEDA weather data and other geological data so that the system can give a more complete picture of the environment Mars.

Multi-objective optimisation of routes. This means that the system can compare different routes to explore based on the terrain, slope, hazards and scientific value. This will allow users to find the fastest route, safest route and scientifically valuable route.

Visualisations to identify hazards in the terrain, geological targets, astronaut telemetry data, simulated Marswalking missions and a dossier to hold information and results from the mission.

2. What are the benefits of your project?

This system is very beneficial as it gives multiple forms of planetary information in one place. It can often be hard to understand how different environmental factors affect each other when planning an exploration mission with separate maps, data and scientific tools. AETHRION aims to make it easier to view the relevant information in one place.

Benefits include:

Increased situational awareness of the terrain, topography, slope and geological data.

Route planning based on different priorities will help show how distance, terrain and scientific objectives can be affected.

Hazards can be identified by seeing steep slopes, cliffs, boulders and other challenging terrain.

Geological targets and sampling sites can be identified to help prioritize the most scientifically valuable areas.

The mission dossier will help organize important information and results from the simulated mission.

The interactive visual environment will help to make complex planetary science information easier to understand.

Overall this shows how planetary science data can be turned into useful information.

3. What impact do you hope to make?

Long term AETHRION will help to make human exploration of Mars safer, more informed and scientifically valuable.

In the future astronauts will be exploring a completely different environment to Earth. This means they will be exploring a planet with a very thin atmosphere, very cold temperatures, challenging terrain and little chance of immediate help from Earth. All of their exploration decisions will need to take into account scientific objectives, resources available, environmental conditions and safety.

AETHRION helps to address this issue by showing how different planetary data sources can be integrated.

This will help bridge the gap between gathering planetary science data and how it can be used in real life situations. The science information will help the user understand how it relates to an actual exploration mission.

Whilst this is just a prototype and simulation, it shows how this concept can be developed by using higher resolution data, more detailed terrain analysis, accurate environmental models and more mission planning tools.

Ultimately we hope to help change how future explorers understand, plan and navigate the Martian surface.

4. What tools, languages, hardware and software have you used?

AETHRION // MARS is a browser based interactive web application. It uses front-end web development, interactive visualisations, planetary science data and route planning concepts.

Mainly using:

HTML – To create the structure of the web application.

CSS – To create styles, responsive design, layout and animations.

JavaScript – To create interactive elements, interactive interface, data and application.

GitHub – For version control.

GitHub Pages – To host the project as a website.

NASA planetary science data – To provide science data for the terrain, topography, images and environmental data.

Pathfinding – Used as the basis for multi-objective route planning.

Visualisations – Web based.

This doesn’t need any specific hardware to run, as it simply uses a modern web browser.

5. How is your project creative and innovative?

AETHRION is creative as it combines planetary exploration, science visualisation and mission planning.

Many planetary visualisation tools can often just present maps or individual science data. AETHRION provides a mission based experience, making the user feel like they are an astronaut exploring Mars in the future. The user can plan an exploration mission by choosing where to land, viewing environmental conditions, identifying hazards, finding scientific targets, planning a Marswalk and seeing the results from their mission.

The system also has multiple route planning priorities. The shortest route may not always be the best for an astronaut to take. Sometimes a longer route may have better terrain or provide access to scientifically valuable geological features. The system provides fastest, safest and scientifically valuable routes to show how the mission planning needs to balance multiple objectives.

The immersive planetary explorer also makes this project more engaging. The user can explore Mars in a more engaging way by moving away from traditional dashboards and providing an interactive visualisation. They can explore landmarks and also enter a dedicated mission control environment.

Overall this system is much more than a basic educational website as it combines an interactive planetary experience with integrated science data, terrain intelligence and route planning. It is a prototype for an integrated planetary mission planning environment.

6. What considerations have we made?

We made consideration of the following factors:

1. Safety for the astronauts – We considered hazards such as steep slopes, cliffs, unstable terrain and challenging geographical features.

2. Accuracy – We used existing NASA planetary science missions and instruments. We considered using multiple data types such as images, topography and environmental data to provide more informative exploration.

3. Multiple objectives for the mission – We considered that exploration isn’t just about getting there as fast as possible. We wanted to show that it’s important to balance route efficiency, terrain, scientific opportunities and getting back safely.

4. Environmental conditions – Mars has extreme temperatures, low pressure, dust and more. We considered this when creating the mission control and astronaut telemetry.

5. Engagement – We created an engaging interface with a cinematic introduction to Mars, interactive exploration tools and organized mission planning.

6. Accessible – We created a web based system so users and evaluators can easily explore the capabilities without having to install any specialist software.

7. Scalable – We created a concept that can be expanded upon with more NASA data, more detailed terrain, improved routing and more mission planning tools.

7. Conclusion

AETHRION // MARS is our attempt to overcome one of the main challenges of future human space exploration. Turning the vast amounts of science information gathered about Mars into useful intelligence to help astronauts on the surface.

By combining planetary exploration, NASA science data, terrain analysis, route planning, hazard awareness and mission reporting we hope to show how technology can help make future Mars exploration more informed, efficient and scientifically valuable.

Our vision is simple, explore the terrain, understand the environment, navigate the unknown and help humanity prepare for their next giant leap!
